spec_match.rationale: Exercises the exact (display-state: normal|minimized|maximized|fullscreen) media feature with MediaQueryList change listeners, correctly notes it is not permission-gated, and explicitly refuses to treat query-text serialization as feature detection.

interactive.rationale: Live four-row .matches table with change listeners, a mock window restyled by @media (display-state: maximized), and separate Fullscreen API enter/exit buttons that are honestly labelled as a different API.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises a live read-out across all four values updated by a change listener; the page delivers the table, the badge, and the titlebar-swap framing.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the no-value-matches unsupported context with an explicit non-established-support message, guards addEventListener in try/catch, exits fullscreen on pagehide, and keeps :fullscreen feedback clearly separated from display-state evidence.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5201832664629248 and the three sibling concept pages.

conformance.rationale: The suite's display-state-reports-an-active-value script and the blocked manual change-event assertion match this page's contract; the fail in this Chromium 141 session is the expected absent experimental media feature, and the page's own copy predicts exactly that outcome.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP verification (no chrome-devtools-mcp here): desktop screenshot shows all four rows false with the honest 'no display-state value matches' message and the n/a badge, zero console errors; fullscreen buttons and a genuine state flip could not be driven non-interactively.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry.assert reports the observed active value and per-row matches, plus the separate fullscreen state on fullscreenchange.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout; the table header uses --text-black on --bg-ivory inverse pairing and buttons override both background and color.

accessibility.rationale: The results table carries an aria-label, state is conveyed as text (true/false plus an explicit status line), and both native buttons have focus-visible outlines.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 shows 0px horizontal overflow with the two-column table fitting the narrow viewport and legible wrapped banner text; desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Record a real display-state change-event transition in an implementing window
openQuestions.detail: The change-listener behaviour — the page's headline mechanism — can only fire in an installed desktop PWA with the AWC flag where the OS actually flips window state; in a browser tab all four rows are false forever. When a flagged installable environment is available, maximize/restore the app window and capture the row flip plus the badge update as evidence, feeding the blocked display-state-change-fires-on-window-state-flip manual conformance assertion.

summary: Clean live read-out of the display-state media feature with honest unsupported-context messaging, a strict separation between :fullscreen feedback and display-state evidence, and no fake detection via query serialization. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this cloud session): all rows honestly false in this unflagged build, zero console errors, no unintended failed requests, no overflow at mobile 360×740 or desktop 1280×800. The change-event transition itself needs an implementing installed window to observe.
